name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
summary: Adversaries with privileged network access may seek to modify network traffic in real time using adversary-in-the-middle (AiTM) attacks. This type of attack allows the adversary to intercept traffic to and/or from a particular device on the network. If a AiTM attack is established, then the adversary has the ability to block, log, modify, or inject traffic into the communication stream. analytics.name: Analytic 1896
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies an Industrial Control System (ICS) Windows host simultaneously holding connections to both the field device subnet and an unexpected external or inter-zone destination, combined with proxy-capable process spawning and ICS vendor application logs showing endpoint or certificate changes. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the asset's documented role does not permit the connection and the destination/proxy/service is outside the approved communications profile, with process/service identity used as corroboration where available. Suppress approved vendor support, update repositories, remote operations, failover paths, and documented temporary…

analytics.name: Analytic 2115
analytics.guidance: Real-time monitoring identifies a process on an Industrial Control System (ICS) Linux asset with both a listening socket on an ICS protocol port and an outbound connection to a non-ICS destination, combined with iptables DNAT rules redirecting ICS protocol port traffic. OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the asset's documented role does not permit the connection and the destination/proxy/service is outside the approved communications profile, with process/service identity used as corroboration where available. Suppress approved vendor support, update repositories, remote operations, failover paths, and documented temporary connectivity.
